texts: Welcome to Quiz Rush! Today we're going to space! Forty real photos of planets, moons, galaxies and more. You have ten seconds each. Ready for lift-off? Let's play!
Kick-off! Which planet is this?
Yes! It's Saturn. Saturn is so light it could float in water, in a big enough bathtub.
Take a good look. Which planet is this?
That's Earth. This famous photo was taken by the Apollo 17 crew in 1972.
Easy one... or is it? What is this?
It's the Moon. The Moon drifts about 3.8 centimetres further from Earth every year.
Eyes on the screen. Which planet is this?
Correct answer: Jupiter. Its Great Red Spot is a storm bigger than Earth.
Quick! Which planet is this?
Of course, it's Mars. Mars has the tallest volcano in the solar system, Olympus Mons.
Trust your instinct. What is this?
Boom! It's the Sun. The Sun holds over 99 percent of the mass of the solar system.
Don't overthink it. What is this?
Here it is: the International Space Station. The ISS circles Earth about every 90 minutes.
This one is a classic. Which is the closest planet to the Sun?
You got it, it's Mercury. A year on Mercury lasts only 88 Earth days.
Here we go. What do we call a space rock that lands on Earth?
Spot on! It's a meteorite. Most meteorites come from the asteroid belt.
Last easy one! What is the name of our galaxy?
The answer is the Milky Way. Our galaxy contains between 100 and 400 billion stars.
Medium round! Things get trickier. Which planet is this?
Yes! It's Neptune. Neptune has the fastest winds in the solar system.
Look closely. Which planet is this?
That's Uranus. Uranus was the first planet discovered with a telescope, in 1781.
Ten seconds on the clock. Which planet is this?
It's Venus. Venus is the hottest planet, even hotter than Mercury.
This one fools a lot of people. What kind of object is this?
Correct answer: a comet. A comet's tail always points away from the Sun.
Can you get this one right? What is this light show called?
Of course, it's an aurora. Auroras happen when particles from the Sun hit our atmosphere.
Think carefully. Which telescope is this?
Boom! It's the Hubble Space Telescope. Hubble was launched in 1990.
Here's a tricky one. What is this event called?
Here it is: a total solar eclipse. A total solar eclipse can last up to about seven and a half minutes.
Keep that streak going! What is Saturn's largest moon?
You got it, it's Titan. Titan is the only moon with a thick atmosphere.
Next up. What kind of space rock is this?
Spot on! It's an asteroid, called Eros. Eros was the first asteroid a spacecraft landed on, in 2001.
Last medium question! Which dwarf planet is this?
The answer is Pluto. Pluto has a heart-shaped glacier called Tombaugh Regio.
Hard round! Only the experts from here. Which moon of Jupiter is this?
Yes! It's Io. Io is the most volcanically active world in the solar system.
Not so easy now. Which moon is this?
That's Europa. Scientists think a salty ocean lies under its icy crust.
Here's one for the experts. Which nebula is this?
It's the Crab Nebula. It's what remains of a star that exploded in 1054.
Take your time... but not too much. Which galaxy is this?
Correct answer: the Andromeda Galaxy. It will collide with the Milky Way in about 4.5 billion years.
This one is a real head-scratcher. Which Mars rover is this?
Of course, it's Curiosity. Curiosity landed on Mars in 2012.
Big brain time! Which moon is this?
Boom! It's Enceladus. Enceladus shoots jets of water ice into space.
Lock in your answer! Which nebula is this?
Here it is: the Orion Nebula. You can see it with the naked eye, just below Orion's Belt.
Few people get this one. Which moon of Saturn is this?
You got it, it's Mimas. Its giant Herschel crater is about a third of its width.
Are you still with me? Which space station is this?
Spot on! It's Mir. Mir orbited Earth for 15 years, from 1986 to 2001.
Last hard one! Which rocket is this?
The answer is the Saturn V. The Saturn V rocket carried astronauts to the Moon.
Genius round! Only true masters get these. Which moon is this?
Yes! It's Triton. Triton orbits Neptune backwards.
Seriously tough now. Which galaxy is this?
That's the Whirlpool Galaxy. It's being pulled by a smaller companion galaxy.
If you know this one, you're a legend. Which nebula is this?
It's the Ring Nebula. It's a cloud of gas thrown off by a dying star.
Deep cut! Which dwarf planet is this?
Correct answer: Ceres. Ceres is the largest object in the asteroid belt.
Here's a rare one. Which comet is this?
Of course, it's comet 67P. The Rosetta mission landed a probe on it in 2014.
No hints this time. Which galaxy is this?
Boom! It's the Sombrero Galaxy. Its bright core is circled by a dark lane of dust.
Almost there! Which moon of Uranus is this?
Here it is: Miranda. Miranda has cliffs about 20 kilometres high.
Only a handful of people will get this. Which moon is this?
You got it, it's Callisto. Callisto is one of the most cratered worlds in the solar system.
Second to last! Which nebula is this?
Spot on! It's the Horsehead Nebula. It lies in the constellation of Orion.
Final question! Make it count. Which asteroid is this?
The answer is Vesta. Vesta is the brightest asteroid seen from Earth.
Mission complete! How many did you get right? Drop your score in the comments, and come back tomorrow, there's a brand new quiz every day on Quiz Rush!
